types.name: Situation reaction (on duty)
types.description: You are placed in a work or public role ("You are an administrative officer…", "You see an accident…") and choose the most responsible, ethical or lawful action.

types.name: Emotional intelligence
types.description: A personal situation (failure, criticism, anger, stress, pressure) asks for the most mature way to handle your own feelings.

types.name: Social intelligence
types.description: A situation with classmates, colleagues, neighbours or a team asks how best to get along, include others, resolve a conflict or lead.

types.name: Critical thinking and logic
types.description: A short claim, rule or argument asks what is definitely true, what weakens or strengthens it, or which argument is strong.

types.name: Eligibility and rule-based decisions
types.description: A list of conditions (eligibility criteria, rules) is followed by a case, and you decide whether the person qualifies or what action the rules require.

types.name: Quick arithmetic puzzles
types.description: A short arithmetic word problem (percentage, ratio, speed, work, profit, interest) appears in the reasoning section.
